title: Infinite cardinal arithmetic: sums, products, and powers
summary: Infinite sums and products can preserve size, while power sets always make it larger.
abstract: The natural numbers can be matched one to one with all ordered pairs of natural numbers, so an infinite square need not be larger than either side. Assuming the axiom of choice, the same phenomenon holds for every infinite set. It implies that adding or multiplying two infinite cardinalities gives the larger one. Powers count functions instead, and the result can be strictly larger: subsets correspond to binary-valued functions, and Cantor’s theorem says there are always more subsets than elements. In particular, the real numbers have the same cardinality as all subsets of the natural numbers.
